title: Find Minimum Element
prompt: Given an array of integers, find and return the smallest value in the array.

steps: Initialize minVal with the first element of the array.
Iterate through the array starting from the second element.
Compare each element with minVal and update minVal if smaller.
Return minVal after checking all elements.
approach.example: For input [5, 2, 8, 1], minVal updates from 5 to 2, then stays 2, then updates to 1, returning 1.

walkthroughSteps: Initialize minVal with nums[0] assuming array is non-empty.
Loop index i from 1 to nums.length - 1 to check remaining elements.
Update minVal whenever nums[i] is smaller than current minVal.
Return minVal after completing array traversal.
commonMistakes: Initializing minVal to 0 instead of the first array element nums[0].
Starting loop at index 0 which does a redundant first comparison.

title: Count Even Numbers
prompt: Given an array of integers, count and return how many numbers are even.

steps: Initialize a counter variable to zero.
Loop through every number in the array.
Check if the number is divisible by two using modulo.
Increment counter if divisible and return total count.
approach.example: For input [1, 2, 3, 4], count becomes 1 at element 2, then 2 at element 4, returning 2.

walkthroughSteps: Initialize count variable to 0 to keep track of even numbers.
Use an enhanced for loop to inspect each integer num in nums.
Apply the modulo operator num % 2 to test for evenness.
Increment count on even numbers and return count at the end.
commonMistakes: Using num % 2 == 1 which fails to catch negative even numbers.
Forgetting to increment count inside the conditional block.

title: Sum Array Elements
prompt: Given an array of integers, calculate and return the sum of all elements.

steps: Initialize accumulator variable total to zero.
Traverse through each integer in the array.
Add the current integer to total.
Return total after visiting all elements.
approach.example: For input [3, 1, 4], total changes from 0 to 3, then 4, then 8, returning 8.

walkthroughSteps: Declare and initialize total variable with zero.
Iterate over nums array using enhanced for-loop syntax.
Add each num value directly to total accumulator.
Return the aggregated total value.
commonMistakes: Initializing total inside the loop body which resets it every step.
Potential integer overflow if array contains extremely large values.

title: Reverse a String
prompt: Given a string, return a new string with its characters in reverse order.

steps: Initialize a StringBuilder object for efficient string construction.
Loop backwards from the last character index down to zero.
Append each character to the StringBuilder.
Convert StringBuilder to String and return it.
approach.example: For input 'cat', loop appends 't', then 'a', then 'c', returning 'tac'.

walkthroughSteps: Create a StringBuilder instance named reversed to avoid String immutability overhead.
Set starting loop counter i to text.length() - 1 for zero-indexed end position.
Append text.charAt(i) to reversed on each decrementing iteration.
Return the finalized string using reversed.toString().
commonMistakes: Using String concatenation inside loop causing O(n^2) performance.
Setting initial index to text.length() resulting in StringIndexOutOfBoundsException.

title: Check String Palindrome
prompt: Determine whether a given string reads the same forwards and backwards.

steps: Initialize left pointer at zero and right pointer at string length minus one.
Loop while left pointer is less than right pointer.
Compare characters at left and right indices.
Return false on mismatch, or true if pointers meet without mismatch.
approach.example: For input 'racecar', left at 'r' and right at 'r' match, moving inward until meeting at 'e', returning true.

walkthroughSteps: Set left pointer to 0 and right pointer to last character index.
Execute while loop as long as left index is less than right index.
Check equality of characters at current pointers using text.charAt().
Advance left pointer rightward and right pointer leftward after each match.
commonMistakes: Comparing characters using == on String objects instead of primitive char comparison.
Forgetting to increment left or decrement right, creating an infinite loop.

title: Count Vowels in String
prompt: Given a string, count and return the total number of vowels it contains.

steps: Initialize count variable to zero and define reference string of vowels.
Loop through each character of the target string.
Check if current character exists within the vowels reference string.
Increment count for matches and return total count.
approach.example: For input 'Hello', 'e' matches (+1), 'o' matches (+1), returning total 2.

walkthroughSteps: Initialize count to track total matched vowels.
Define vowels string containing both uppercase and lowercase vowel chars.
Iterate through text indices using standard for loop.
Use vowels.indexOf() to check if current char is present in vowels set.
commonMistakes: Checking only lowercase vowels and ignoring uppercase vowels.
Using text.length instead of text.length() for String length access.

title: Find Maximum Element
prompt: Given an array of integers, find and return the largest value in the array.

steps: Initialize maxVal with the first element of the array.
Iterate through array elements starting from index one.
Compare each element with maxVal and update maxVal if larger.
Return maxVal after evaluating all elements.
approach.example: For input [3, 9, 2], maxVal starts at 3, updates to 9 at element 9, then stays 9, returning 9.

walkthroughSteps: Assign first element nums[0] to maxVal as baseline comparison.
Traverse array elements from index 1 to length - 1.
Update maxVal whenever nums[i] exceeds current maxVal.
Return maxVal after checking every index.
commonMistakes: Initializing maxVal to 0 which fails when all array numbers are negative.
Off-by-one error using i <= nums.length in the loop condition.

title: Calculate Factorial
prompt: Given a non-negative integer, calculate and return its factorial value.

steps: Initialize product result variable to long integer one.
Loop integer i from two up to n inclusive.
Multiply result by current multiplier i.
Return result after loop completion.
approach.example: For input 4, result multiplies 1 * 2 = 2, then * 3 = 6, then * 4 = 24, returning 24.

walkthroughSteps: Use long data type for result to reduce integer overflow risk.
Initialize result to 1 to handle n equal to 0 or 1 correctly.
Iterate from 2 up to n inclusive, accumulating products.
Return computed result.
commonMistakes: Initializing result to 0 which causes all multiplications to yield 0.
Using int instead of long causing early overflow for n greater than 12.

title: Check Prime Number
prompt: Given a positive integer greater than one, determine whether it is a prime number.

steps: Return false immediately if n is less than or equal to one.
Iterate divisor i starting from two while i squared is less than or equal to n.
Return false if n is evenly divisible by i.
Return true if no divisors are found.
approach.example: For input 7, tests divisor 2 (2*2 <= 7), 7%2 != 0, loop ends and returns true.

walkthroughSteps: Filter out numbers less than or equal to 1 which are non-prime.
Check potential divisors up to square root of n using i * i <= n.
Return false immediately upon finding any divisor where n % i == 0.
Return true after verifying no factors exist up to square root.
commonMistakes: Checking factors up to n instead of sqrt(n), causing O(n) performance.
Treating 1 as a prime number.

title: Linear Search
prompt: Given an array of integers and a target value, return the index of target or negative one if absent.

steps: Loop through the array elements using index counter i.
Compare value at index i with target.
Return index i immediately if value matches target.
Return negative one if loop completes without finding target.
approach.example: For input [10, 20, 30] and target 20, index 0 is 10, index 1 matches 20, returning 1.

walkthroughSteps: Iterate through nums array index by index from 0 to nums.length - 1.
Check equality between nums[i] and target value.
Return current index i on first matching value found.
Return -1 outside loop signaling target was not present in array.
commonMistakes: Returning -1 inside the loop after the first non-matching element.
Returning target value instead of element index i.

title: Find Array Average
prompt: Given an array of integers, calculate and return the average value as a double.

steps: Initialize double precision variable sum to zero point zero.
Traverse through all elements in the array and add them to sum.
Divide sum by array length.
Return calculated average double value.
approach.example: For input [2, 4, 6], sum accumulates to 12.0, divided by length 3 yields 4.0.

walkthroughSteps: Declare sum variable as type double to enforce floating-point division.
Accumulate each array element into double precision sum variable.
Divide sum by nums.length to compute mean value.
Return double floating-point result.
commonMistakes: Using int for sum variable causing integer truncation during division.
Dividing by zero without checking for empty array input.

title: Check Contains Duplicate
prompt: Given an array of integers, determine if any value appears at least twice.

steps: Initialize empty HashSet to track unique elements visited.
Iterate through each number in array.
Check if HashSet already contains current number.
Return true if duplicate found, else add to set and return false at end.
approach.example: For input [1, 2, 3, 1], set stores {1, 2, 3}, at second 1 set.contains(1) is true, returning true.

walkthroughSteps: Instantiate HashSet named seen for O(1) average lookup time.
Iterate over nums array using enhanced for loop.
Call seen.contains(num) to inspect prior element encounters.
Add unseen element to set via seen.add(num) or return true on match.
commonMistakes: Nested loop approach giving O(n^2) runtime instead of using HashSet.
Adding num to set before checking if it already exists.

title: Fizz Buzz Single Number
prompt: Given an integer, return Fizz if divisible by three, Buzz if by five, FizzBuzz if both, or string representation.

steps: Check if number is divisible by fifteen first.
Check if number is divisible by three next.
Check if number is divisible by five next.
Return number converted to string if none of above match.
approach.example: For input 15, modulo 15 check matches first, returning string FizzBuzz.

walkthroughSteps: Test n % 15 == 0 first to catch numbers divisible by both 3 and 5.
Test n % 3 == 0 conditional for numbers only divisible by 3.
Test n % 5 == 0 conditional for numbers only divisible by 5.
Convert integer n to String via String.valueOf(n) as fallback.
commonMistakes: Checking n % 3 before n % 15 causing multiples of 15 to incorrectly return 'Fizz'.
Using string concatenation without returning or chaining conditionals correctly.

title: Find Nth Fibonacci Number
prompt: Given a non-negative integer n, calculate and return the nth Fibonacci number.

steps: Return n directly if n is zero or one base case.
Initialize prev to zero and curr to one.
Loop from two up to n updating prev and curr.
Return curr after loop completes.
approach.example: For input 3, loop running for i=2 gives next=1 (prev=1, curr=1), for i=3 gives next=2 (prev=1, curr=2), returning 2.

walkthroughSteps: Handle base cases n = 0 and n = 1 by returning n directly.
Maintain state of previous two numbers using prev and curr variables.
Compute sum next = prev + curr and shift pointers forward inside loop.
Return final curr value representing F(n).
commonMistakes: Using naive recursion causing exponential O(2^n) execution time.
Incorrect variable swapping order resulting in corrupted terms.

title: Count Target Occurrences
prompt: Given an array of integers and a target value, return how many times target appears in the array.

steps: Initialize match count variable to zero.
Iterate over each integer element in the array.
Compare element with target and increment count on match.
Return total count after iteration.
approach.example: For input [1, 2, 2, 3] and target 2, match found twice, returning count 2.

walkthroughSteps: Declare count variable initialized to zero.
Loop through nums array using enhanced for loop.
Check primitive equality num == target for each element.
Return accumulated count upon visiting all elements.
commonMistakes: Returning count prematurely inside loop on first target match.
Using .equals() on primitive int values instead of == operator.

title: Count Words in String
prompt: Given a string of space-separated words, count and return the total number of non-empty words.

steps: Check if the string is null or empty after trimming whitespace.
Split the trimmed string on one or more whitespace characters.
Return the length of the resulting array of words.
approach.example: For input   hello   world  , trim gives 'hello   world', split gives ['hello', 'world'], returning length 2.

walkthroughSteps: Check boundary conditions using text.trim().isEmpty().
Use regular expression split('\s+) to split across multiple spaces.
Return array length representing word count.
commonMistakes: Splitting by single space
which creates empty array entries for multiple spaces.
Forgetting to handle null or empty string input, causing NullPointerException.

title: Check Valid Anagram
prompt: Given two strings s and t, determine if t is an anagram of s containing the exact same character frequencies.

steps: Return false immediately if string lengths are unequal.
Create an array of size 26 to store character frequency counts.
Iterate through strings, incrementing count for s and decrementing for t.
Return true if all array counts are zero, else false.
approach.example: For s = 'listen' and t = 'silent', character counts balance to zero for every character, returning true.

walkthroughSteps: Verify s and t have matching lengths as initial check.
Maintain fixed-size frequency array for lowercase alphabet chars.
Simultaneously add s characters and subtract t characters.
Validate that every frequency value returns back to zero.
commonMistakes: Sorting both strings which increases time complexity to O(n log n).
Not accounting for length mismatch before starting iteration.

title: Find Missing Number
prompt: Given an array containing n distinct numbers in the range zero to n, find the single missing number.

steps: Calculate expected sum of numbers from 0 to n using arithmetic sum formula.
Iterate through the input array to sum actual elements present.
Subtract actual sum from expected sum.
Return the resulting difference as the missing number.
approach.example: For [3, 0, 1] (n=3), expected sum is 3*4/2 = 6, actual sum is 4, missing number is 6 - 4 = 2.

walkthroughSteps: Compute expected sum formula n * (n + 1) / 2 using array length n.
Sum array items using single loop traversal.
Compute missing value by calculating expectedSum - actualSum.
commonMistakes: Sorting array first, introducing unnecessary O(n log n) overhead.
Off-by-one errors in formula multiplier using length instead of n + 1.

title: Move Zeroes to End
prompt: Given an array of integers, modify it in-place so all zeroes are moved to the end while maintaining relative element order.

steps: Maintain insertPos pointer tracking position for non-zero values.
Iterate array, placing non-zero values at insertPos and incrementing pointer.
Fill remaining indices from insertPos to array length with zeroes.
approach.example: For [0, 1, 0, 3], array becomes [1, 3, 0, 3] after non-zero copy, then second loop sets remaining indices to [1, 3, 0, 0].

walkthroughSteps: Use insertPos index pointer starting at 0.
Overwrite initial elements with non-zero values while advancing pointer.
Zero out all array indices from final insertPos up to nums.length.
commonMistakes: Creating auxiliary array which breaks O(1) space constraint.
Swapping elements without preserving relative order of non-zero elements.

title: Remove Target Element
prompt: Given an integer array and a target value, remove all instances of target in-place and return the new length.

steps: Initialize pointer index to zero for tracking write position.
Iterate through array checking elements against target.
Write element to write index if not equal to target and increment index.
Return final index value as new valid length.
approach.example: For [3, 2, 2, 3] and target 3, index increments at elements 2 and 2, writing [2, 2] and returning length 2.

walkthroughSteps: Use index as write pointer tracking non-target placement.
Loop through elements, skipping values matching target.
Copy retained values forward and return modified length.
commonMistakes: Trying to resize Java primitive array directly which is impossible.
Decrementing index improperly while modifying array during iteration.

title: Check Power of Two
prompt: Given an integer n, determine whether it is a power of two.

steps: Return false if integer n is less than or equal to zero.
Repeatedly divide n by two while n is even.
Check if final value of n equals one.
Return boolean comparison result.
approach.example: For input 16, divides 16->8->4->2->1, n becomes 1, returning true.

walkthroughSteps: Exclude numbers non-positive as valid power of two candidates.
Divide by 2 iteratively until odd number reached.
Verify remaining factor equals exactly 1.
commonMistakes: Handling negative numbers or zero incorrectly.
Infinite loop if n /= 2 division condition is misconfigured.

title: Binary Search Sorted Array
prompt: Given a sorted integer array and target, find index of target using binary search or return negative one.

steps: Initialize left pointer to zero and right pointer to array length minus one.
Calculate middle index while left is less than or equal to right.
Adjust search bounds based on comparison between middle element and target.
Return mid index on match, or negative one if left exceeds right.
approach.example: For [-1, 0, 3, 5, 9, 12] and target 9, mid visits 3 (val 5), shifts right, mid visits index 4 (val 9), returning 4.

walkthroughSteps: Initialize boundary pointers left = 0 and right = length - 1.
Calculate mid using left + (right - left) / 2 to prevent integer overflow.
Shrink search interval by updating left or right boundaries.
Return target mid index or -1 if target not found.
commonMistakes: Using (left + right) / 2 which risks potential integer overflow.
Using left < right condition missing single element match checking.

title: First Unique Character
prompt: Given a string, find the index of its first non-repeating character, or return negative one if none exists.

steps: Populate character frequency map using fixed-size array.
Iterate through string characters a second time.
Return index of first character with frequency count of one.
Return negative one if all characters repeat.
approach.example: For input 'leetcode', character 'l' has frequency 1 at index 0, returning 0.

walkthroughSteps: Build count frequencies using array indexing s.charAt(i) - 'a'.
Traverse string second time preserving original character sequence.
Identify first index matching frequency count == 1.
commonMistakes: Nested loop scan leading to O(n^2) time complexity.
Searching frequency array directly which loses character order info.

title: Sum of Digits
prompt: Given a non-negative integer n, calculate and return the sum of its individual digits.

steps: Initialize total variable to zero.
Extract last digit using modulo ten operation.
Add digit to total and remove last digit using integer division by ten.
Repeat until n becomes zero and return total.
approach.example: For input 123, extracts 3 (sum=3, n=12), then 2 (sum=5, n=1), then 1 (sum=6, n=0), returning 6.

walkthroughSteps: Use while loop condition n > 0 to process each digit.
Extract rightmost digit with n % 10 operator.
Truncate rightmost digit using integer division n /= 10.
commonMistakes: Converting integer to string causing extra memory overhead.
Infinite loop by omitting n /= 10 step.

title: Find Second Largest Element
prompt: Given an array of integers, find and return the second largest distinct value in the array.

steps: Initialize variables largest and second to minimum integer value.
Iterate through array elements updating largest and shifting old largest to second.
Update second if current element is smaller than largest but strictly greater than second.
Return final value of second.
approach.example: For [12, 35, 1, 10, 34, 1], largest becomes 35, second becomes 34, returning 34.

walkthroughSteps: Track two state variables largest and second initialized to Integer.MIN_VALUE.
Shift values when encountering new absolute maximum num > largest.
Update second for values between largest and previous second.
Enforce strict inequality num != largest to ignore duplicate maximums.
commonMistakes: Sorting array and taking nums[nums.length - 2] which fails on duplicate max values.
Initializing variables to 0 which fails when input numbers are negative.

title: Merge Two Sorted Arrays
prompt: Given two sorted integer arrays, merge them into a single new sorted array and return it.

steps: Allocate result array with combined length of input arrays.
Use pointers i, j, k to traverse input arrays and destination array.
Compare elements from both arrays, copying smaller element into result array.
Copy remaining elements from whichever array has remaining values.
approach.example: For [1, 3] and [2, 4], compares and copies 1, then 2, then 3, then 4 into [1, 2, 3, 4].

walkthroughSteps: Allocate new result array sized to a.length + b.length.
Iterate simultaneously over both arrays inserting smallest available item.
Append leftover items using individual while loops.
commonMistakes: Concatenating and then sorting, wasting time with O((n+m) log(n+m)).
IndexOutOfBoundsException by accessing indices beyond individual array bounds.

title: Find Array Intersection
prompt: Given two integer arrays, return an array containing their unique common elements.

steps: Add all elements of first array to a HashSet.
Iterate second array, adding matching elements from set into second result set.
Convert result set into primitive integer array and return.
approach.example: For [1, 2, 2, 1] and [2, 2], set1 contains {1, 2}, matched elements added to resultSet yield [2].

walkthroughSteps: Store unique values of nums1 into set1 for fast lookup.
Collect intersecting values into resultSet to ensure result uniqueness.
Populate final primitive integer array from resultSet.
commonMistakes: Including duplicate common elements in output array.
Using nested loops giving O(n * m) runtime.

title: Check Armstrong Number
prompt: Given a non-negative integer, determine if sum of its digits raised to power of digit count equals original number.

steps: Store original number copy and calculate total digit count.
Extract each digit using modulo ten operator.
Raise digit to total digit count power and accumulate sum.
Return whether accumulated sum equals original number.
approach.example: For 153 (3 digits), 1^3 + 5^3 + 3^3 = 1 + 125 + 27 = 153, returning true.

walkthroughSteps: Save initial input value into original variable.
Determine digit length using String.valueOf(n).length().
Accumulate pow(digit, digits) into sum variable.
Verify sum == original comparison.
commonMistakes: Hardcoding digit exponent as 3 instead of dynamically computing length.
Comparing sum with modified variable n instead of saved original value.

title: Valid Parentheses
prompt: Given a string containing only bracket characters, check if every opening bracket has matching closing bracket in order.

steps: Initialize a Character stack for storing open bracket symbols.
Push opening brackets onto stack as encountered.
Pop and compare top bracket on seeing matching closing bracket.
Return true if stack ends completely empty.
approach.example: For '()[]', pushes '(', pops and matches ')', pushes '[', pops and matches ']', returning true.

walkthroughSteps: Use Stack data structure to track bracket nesting order.
Push opening brackets '(', '{', '[' directly onto stack.
Validate closing brackets against pop element from non-empty stack.
Confirm stack is empty at end to handle unmatched opening brackets.
commonMistakes: Calling stack.pop() without checking stack.isEmpty() causing EmptyStackException.
Assuming string is valid without checking final stack empty status.

title: Longest Common Prefix
prompt: Given an array of strings, find and return the longest common prefix shared among all strings.

steps: Initialize prefix variable with first string in array.
Iterate through remaining strings in array.
Shorten prefix string until current string starts with prefix.
Return prefix string or empty string if prefix shrinks to empty.
approach.example: For [flower, flow, flight], prefix starts as flower, shortens to flow, then shortens to fl, returning fl.

walkthroughSteps: Set prefix candidate to initial element strs[0].
Test prefix against each string using strs[i].indexOf(prefix) == 0.
Trim candidate prefix character by character until match occurs.
Return remaining common prefix.
commonMistakes: Not handling empty input array, leading to IndexOutOfBoundsException.
Using character-by-character comparison loops without boundary checking.

title: Max Consecutive Ones
prompt: Given a binary array of zeroes and ones, find and return the maximum number of consecutive ones.

steps: Initialize maxCount and currentCount variables to zero.
Traverse through each binary digit in the array.
Increment currentCount on one, or reset currentCount to zero on zero.
Update maxCount whenever currentCount exceeds maxCount.
approach.example: For input [1, 1, 0, 1, 1, 1], currentCount reaches 2, resets to 0 at 0, then reaches 3, returning maxCount 3.

walkthroughSteps: Track active streak length using currentCount variable.
Update maxCount using Math.max whenever currentCount grows.
Reset currentCount back to zero when encountering a zero element.
Return highest recorded consecutive streak stored in maxCount.
commonMistakes: Forgetting to reset currentCount upon encountering zero.
Updating maxCount only at the end of loop which misses streaks ending mid-array.

title: Check Leap Year
prompt: Given an integer year, determine whether it is a leap year based on calendar division rules.

steps: Check if year is divisible by 400, returning true if so.
Check if year is divisible by 100, returning false if so.
Check if year is divisible by 4, returning true if so.
Return false for all other cases.
approach.example: For input 2000, divisible by 400 returns true. For 1900, divisible by 100 returns false.

walkthroughSteps: Evaluate century leap rule year % 400 == 0 first.
Evaluate century non-leap rule year % 100 == 0 second.
Evaluate standard leap rule year % 4 == 0 third.
Return false for years failing all leap conditions.
commonMistakes: Checking year % 4 == 0 first, incorrectly identifying century years like 1900 as leap years.
Combining conditionals incorrectly leading to reversed logic.

title: Reverse Integer Digits
prompt: Given an integer, reverse its digits and return the newly formed integer value.

steps: Initialize reversed accumulator variable to zero.
Extract last digit using modulo ten operator.
Multiply reversed by ten and add extracted digit.
Divide integer by ten until input becomes zero.
approach.example: For input 123, extracts 3 (reversed=3), then 2 (reversed=32), then 1 (reversed=321), returning 321.

walkthroughSteps: Iterate while n != 0 to properly handle negative integer inputs.
Isolate current last digit with n % 10.
Shift existing digits left by multiplying reversed by 10 and adding digit.
Remove processed digit via n /= 10.
commonMistakes: Using n > 0 condition which fails for negative integer inputs.
Forgetting to multiply existing reversed value by 10 before adding new digit.

title: Find Majority Element
prompt: Given an array of integers, find the majority element that appears more than n / 2 times.

steps: Initialize candidate variable and count counter to zero.
Iterate through array updating candidate when count is zero.
Increment count if element matches candidate, else decrement count.
Return final candidate as majority element.
approach.example: For input [2, 2, 1, 1, 1, 2, 2], Boyer-Moore voting process keeps candidate 2, returning 2.

walkthroughSteps: Apply Boyer-Moore Voting Algorithm logic.
Assign new candidate whenever current count drops to 0.
Adjust balance score count based on matching candidate value.
Return candidate which survives majority cancellation.
commonMistakes: Using HashMap or sorting which increases space to O(n) or time to O(n log n).
Resetting count to 1 instead of continuing voting logic.

title: Find Single Number
prompt: Given a non-empty array of integers where every element appears twice except for one, find that single element.

steps: Initialize result variable to zero.
Iterate through every integer in the array.
Apply bitwise XOR operation between result and current integer.
Return result after loop completion.
approach.example: For input [4, 1, 2, 1, 2], XOR accumulation cancels paired 1s and 2s leaving 4, returning 4.

walkthroughSteps: Leverage XOR property: x ^ x = 0 and x ^ 0 = x.
Traverse nums array applying cumulative XOR result ^= num.
Duplicate numbers cancel each other out to zero.
Return remaining non-canceled single number value.
commonMistakes: Using nested loops resulting in O(n^2) runtime.
Using extra HashSet memory when bit manipulation achieves O(1) space.

title: Rotate Array Left
prompt: Given an integer array, shift all elements left by one position and move the original first element to the last position.

steps: Save the first element of the array into a temporary variable.
Loop from index zero to array length minus two.
Shift each element at index i + 1 leftward to index i.
Place saved temporary element into the last index of the array.
approach.example: For [1, 2, 3, 4], first val 1 saved, elements shifted to [2, 3, 4, 4], 1 placed at end yields [2, 3, 4, 1].

walkthroughSteps: Check base condition nums.length <= 1 to avoid unnecessary array operations.
Preserve nums[0] value inside variable first.
Overwrite each nums[i] with adjacent right element nums[i + 1].
Assign original first element into final index nums[nums.length - 1].
commonMistakes: Overwriting nums[0] before storing it in a temporary variable.
Looping up to length - 1 causing IndexOutOfBoundsException on i + 1.

title: Square Root Floor
prompt: Given a non-negative integer x, calculate and return its square root rounded down to the nearest integer.

steps: Handle base cases 0 and 1 by returning x directly.
Initialize binary search bounds left to 1 and right to x / 2.
Calculate mid and check if mid * mid is less than or equal to x.
Adjust binary search bounds until floor integer root is found.
approach.example: For input 8, binary search evaluates mid values 4, then 2, finding 2 * 2 = 4 <= 8 while 3 * 3 = 9 > 8, returning 2.

walkthroughSteps: Return x directly for 0 and 1 base cases.
Set search range from 1 to x / 2.
Cast mid * mid product to long to avoid integer overflow.
Store candidate valid root in ans before advancing left bound.
commonMistakes: Mid * mid calculation overflowing standard 32-bit signed integer limits.
Using built-in Math.sqrt function instead of implementing integer arithmetic.

title: Check Array Sorted
prompt: Given an array of integers, determine whether it is sorted in non-decreasing order.

steps: Iterate through array from index zero to array length minus two.
Compare current element with adjacent right element.
Return false immediately if current element is strictly greater than right element.
Return true if loop finishes without out-of-order pairs.
approach.example: For [1, 2, 4, 3], comparing 4 and 3 detects 4 > 3, returning false.

walkthroughSteps: Traverse consecutive adjacent pairs using index i and i + 1.
Detect non-decreasing rule violations where nums[i] > nums[i + 1].
Return false immediately upon encountering first inversion.
Return true when all pairs satisfy non-decreasing property.
commonMistakes: Off-by-one loop index bound causing IndexOutOfBoundsException on nums[i + 1].
Using >= comparison which incorrectly flags array with duplicate elements as unsorted.

title: Transpose Matrix
prompt: Given a 2D integer matrix, compute and return a new 2D matrix representing its transpose.

steps: Determine row count r and column count c of input matrix.
Create new destination matrix with swapped dimensions c by r.
Iterate over each row i and column j.
Assign value matrix[i][j] to transpose[j][i].

walkthroughSteps: Read dimensions rows = matrix.length and cols = matrix[0].length.
Allocate result matrix with swapped dimensions int[cols][rows].
Traverse input cells assigning result[j][i] = matrix[i][j].
Return constructed transposed matrix.
commonMistakes: Allocating result with original dimensions int[rows][cols] causing index errors on non-square matrices.
Swapping elements in-place on a non-square matrix.

Append one at the end of list and return finalized row.

walkthroughSteps: Initialize row list with seed element 1.
Outer loop iterates from row 1 up to target rowIndex.
Inner loop computes row values backwards row.get(j) + row.get(j - 1) to avoid overwriting prior calculations.
Append boundary value 1 and return completed row.
commonMistakes: Iterating forward in inner loop which overwrites values needed for subsequent elements.
Off-by-one errors in row index boundaries.
